mainTopic: Does permitted material cancel a forbidden item? רבי שמעון's rule about items that 'have מתירין', the challenge from שביעית, and a new proof from rained-on onions
overview: The גמרא is trying to settle whether permitted material or permitted growth can cancel out a forbidden item. It quotes a ברייתא of רבי שמעון: items that will become permitted later, like טבל or חדש, are never cancelled, but items that stay forbidden forever, like תרומה or ערלה, can be cancelled. The חכמים challenge him from שביעית, which seems to stay forbidden yet forbids its own kind in any amount. רבי שמעון answers that the 'any amount' rule is only about ביעור, while for eating the rule is נותן טעם. The גמרא rejects this as a proof, because a stringent ruling may be different. Next it brings a משנה about onions that sprouted during or after שביעית, which suggests that permitted growth cancels the forbidden original. That proof is pushed away too: maybe the משנה is about crushed onions that are no longer fit to eat. The amud ends as the גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא for a new proof, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's rule: items that will become permitted vs. items that never will
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון teaches that a forbidden item that will become permitted later has no measure for cancelling it, while a forbidden item that will never become permitted does have such a measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any item that can become permitted later, like טבל, מעשר שני, הקדש, and חדש, the חכמים set no measure for cancelling it. Any item that can never become permitted, like תרומה, תרומת מעשר, חלה, ערלה, and כלאי הכרם, the חכמים did set a measure for cancelling it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a ברייתא of רבי שמעון that sorts forbidden foods into two groups. Some can be cancelled when mixed with permitted food, and some cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a forbidden item will become permitted anyway (by tithing, redeeming, or waiting for the עומר), you can just wait and eat it permitted, so it is never cancelled, even in a tiny amount. If it will stay forbidden forever, the חכמים allow it to be cancelled once there is enough permitted food against it. This rule is the background for the challenge that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: An item whose prohibition will go away; it can become permitted later
A set measure or ratio at which the forbidden item is cancelled in a mixture
Produce that has not yet been tithed
New grain, forbidden until the עומר is brought
Fruit of a tree in its first three years
Forbidden crops planted together in a vineyard

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards at first. The item that will become permitted is treated more strictly, because there is no need to rely on cancelling it when you can simply wait.

phrases.english: Any item that can become permitted,
for example, untithed produce and second tithe
and consecrated items and new grain,
the Sages did not set a measure for them.
phrases.notes: So any amount of them, even tiny, forbids the mixture.

phrases.english: And any item that cannot become permitted,
for example, teruma and teruma of the tithe
and challa, and orla, and forbidden crops in a vineyard,
the Sages set a measure for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that the גמרא had already started quoting before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items with מתירין are never cancelled; items without מתירין have a set measure for cancelling.

steps.title: The חכמים challenge רבי שמעון from שביעית produce
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים point out that שביעית produce never becomes permitted, yet it is never cancelled. This seems to break רבי שמעון's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But שביעית produce cannot become permitted, and still the חכמים set no measure for it, as the משנה says: שביעית produce forbids any amount of its own kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים attack רבי שמעון's rule with a counter-example. שביעית seems to belong to the 'never permitted' group, but it behaves like the 'will be permitted' group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבי שמעון's rule, an item with no מתירין should have a measure for cancelling. A משנה, though, says שביעית forbids its own kind in any amount, meaning it has no measure. So either the rule is wrong or שביעית needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce of the Sabbatical (seventh) year, which has special holiness
Any amount at all, even the tiniest bit
With its own kind (mixed with the same type of food)
But isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא שְׁבִיעִית אֵין לָהּ מַתִּירִין,
phrases.english: They said to him: But doesn't Sabbatical-year produce have no way to become permitted,
phrases.notes: 'They' are the חכמים arguing with רבי שמעון inside the same ברייתא.

phrases.english: and yet the Sages did not set a measure for it.
As we learned: Sabbatical-year produce forbids
in any amount with its own kind!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא שְׁבִיעִית אֵין לָהּ מַתִּירִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule just stated in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's rule that items without מתירין have a measure for cancelling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counter-example: שביעית has no מתירין, yet a משנה says it forbids in any amount.

steps.title: רבי שמעון answers: 'any amount' applies only to removal; for eating it is flavor
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון explains that the 'any amount' rule for שביעית is only about ביעור. For eating, the rule is נותן טעם, so there is a measure after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I too only said this about ביעור. But about eating, it is forbidden only if it gives taste.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון defends his rule by limiting the משנה about שביעית. The strict 'any amount' rule only applies to one area, ביעור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the time of ביעור, שביעית produce may be eaten, so in that period it is like an item that will be permitted, and it has no measure. After ביעור, when eating is forbidden, it is cancelled unless it gives taste, which fits his rule. The גמרא hopes this shows that permitted material can cancel the forbidden item.

keyTerms.meaning: The time when שביעית produce must be removed from one's house, once that kind is gone from the fields
Gives taste; forbidden only if the forbidden item flavors the mixture
I too; I agree with you on that point

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: אַף אֲנִי לֹא אָמַרְתִּי
phrases.english: He said to them: I too said this only
regarding removal.
phrases.notes: Before ביעור you may eat it, so in that period it counts as something that has מתירין.

phrases.english: But regarding eating, the measure is if it gives taste.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: אַף אֲנִי לֹא אָמַרְתִּי אֶלָּא לְבִיעוּר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the cited משנה (applies only to ביעור).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים thought שביעית always forbids in any amount.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only regarding ביעור is there no measure; for eating, the measure is נותן טעם, matching רבי שמעון's rule.

steps.title: The proof is rejected: a stringent case may be different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe this case only shows something when the result is strict, so it proves nothing for a lenient result.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe here too, a stringent ruling is different!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the attempt to use רבי שמעון's ברייתא as a proof. It says the case may be special because it leads to a strict result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'too' tells us the גמרא already rejected an earlier proof the same way. A rule applied to make things stricter cannot be used to prove the same rule when it would make things more lenient. So the גמרא looks for a new proof in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps; introduces a rejection
In the direction of strictness
It is different

phrases.english: But perhaps here too,
phrases.notes: 'Too' points back to an earlier proof that the גמרא pushed away for the same reason.

phrases.english: a stringency is different!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof drawn from steps 1-3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from רבי שמעון's ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case involves a stringency, so it cannot prove the rule in a lenient case.

steps.title: A new proof from onions that sprouted in the Sabbatical year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a different source to settle the question: a משנה about sixth-year onions that grew new sprouts after rain fell on them in שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he settled it from this source, as we learned: Onions that had rain fall on them and they sprouted: if their leaves were dark, they are forbidden. If the leaves turned pale, they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: After the last proof failed, the גמרא brings a new source to answer the question. It quotes a משנה about onions, and this sets up the proof that will be explained next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dark leaves show fresh growth during שביעית, so the onions are forbidden as שביעית produce. Pale, withered-looking leaves show the onion is still mainly the old sixth-year onion, so it is permitted. The גמרא will use this to learn how new growth relates to the original item.

keyTerms.meaning: He resolved it (settled the question)
Onions
Dark (deep green), a sign of fresh growth
Turned pale or yellowish, looking withered

phrases.english: Rather, he resolved it from this, as we learned:
phrases.notes: 'He' is ישמעאל איש כפר ימא, who asked this question on the previous amud. The משנה is שביעית 6:3.

phrases.english: Onions on which rain fell and they sprouted,
phrases.notes: These are onions from the sixth year that started growing again during שביעית.

phrases.english: if their leaves were
dark, they are forbidden.
If they turned pale, they are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof of step 4 with a new source.
steps.raayaObject: The open question of whether permitted material or new growth can cancel the forbidden original.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה שביעית 6:3 about onions that sprouted in שביעית.

steps.title: The rest of the onion משנה: pulled up by their leaves
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנניא בן אנטיגנוס gives a test: if the onions can be pulled up by their leaves, they are forbidden. In the reverse case, after שביעית ends, they are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנניא בן אנטיגנוס says: If the onions can be pulled out of the ground by holding their leaves, they are forbidden. And in the reverse case, after שביעית is over, they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of the משנה it started in the last step. The key part for our question is the last line: in the reverse case, after שביעית, the onions are permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strong leaves mean a lot of new growth happened during שביעית, so the onions are forbidden. The reverse case is onions from שביעית that grew new leaves in the eighth year, and those are permitted. That last line is what the גמרא will try to use as a proof in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Can be pulled up by their leaves. This is a sign that the leaves are strong and full of new growth.
The matching case going the other way: the reverse case.
The time right after שביעית ends, meaning the eighth year.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chananya ben Antigonos says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יְכוֹלִין לִיתָּלֵשׁ בֶּעָלִין שֶׁלָּהֶן — אֲסוּרִין.
phrases.english: If they can be pulled up by their leaves, they are forbidden.
And in the reverse case, at the end of the Seventh Year, they are permitted.
phrases.notes: Here the onions themselves are from שביעית, and the new growth came in the eighth year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and completes the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: Whether permitted growth cancels the original prohibition.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about onions and שביעית, especially the line about the time after שביעית.

steps.title: Proposed proof: permitted growth cancels the prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה proves גידולי היתר מעלין את האיסור, meaning permitted growth cancels the forbidden original.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that permitted growth cancels the prohibition?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a lesson from the משנה: since onions from שביעית become permitted once they grow in the eighth year, maybe permitted growth cancels the original prohibition. This is only a proposal, and the next step pushes back on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original onion was forbidden because it came from שביעית. Only the new growth in the eighth year is permitted, yet the whole onion is permitted. So it seems the permitted new part outweighs and cancels the forbidden original part.

keyTerms.meaning: Does this mean that? The גמרא uses it to draw a lesson from a source.
Permitted growth: new growth that is not forbidden.
Cancel the prohibition. Literally, 'lift up' the forbidden part.

phrases.english: Does this mean that permitted growth
cancels the prohibition?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּגִידּוּלֵי הֶיתֵּר מַעֲלִין אֶת הָאִיסּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the last line of the משנה in step 6.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling that onions from שביעית that grew in the eighth year are permitted.

steps.title: Maybe the משנה is about crushed onions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: maybe the משנה is talking about crushed onions, so the reason they are permitted is something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps the משנה is talking about crushed onions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof it just suggested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה is about crushed onions, the original שביעית onion is ruined and no longer fit to eat, so it does not count anymore. That would be the reason the onion is permitted, not that the new growth cancels the original. So the משנה proves nothing about גידולי היתר מעלין את האיסור, and step 9 starts a new attempt.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps. This is a common way for the גמרא to push back on a proof.
Crushed or pounded, like something ground in a mortar.

phrases.english: But perhaps it is talking about crushed onions.
phrases.notes: If so, the onions are permitted because of something special about crushed onions, not because of the new growth.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from this משנה. The question itself is still open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה may be talking about a special case, crushed onions, where the reason for the permission is different.

steps.title: Setting up a new proof from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the onion proof and announces that it will bring a different source, a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn it from this source, as it is taught in a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready to quote a ברייתא as a new proof, and the ברייתא itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא tells us the earlier proof was rejected. The גמרא is starting a fresh try to answer the same question: does permitted growth cancel the prohibition?

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It tells us the last idea was dropped and a new one is coming.
From this one, meaning this source.
As it is taught in a ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself.

phrases.english: Rather, learn it from this source,
as it is taught in a ברייתא:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in step 7 was rejected in step 8, the גמרא opens a new source.
steps.raayaObject: Whether גידולי היתר מעלין את האיסור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא, which is quoted in the next part of the text.
